preamble: larder: a self-hosted, FLOSS household food system (recipes, weekly dinner planning, shared shopping list; later, pantry estimates driven by receipts). Specs: docs/goals.md, docs/requirements.md, docs/specs/, docs/decisions/. Slices titled "Interview:" collect the owner's decisions and come before the slices that depend on them. Every slice has an "Owner input" section listing what to confirm before starting. Household-specific answers go in the gitignored local/ folder, never in committed files.

items.title: Interview: device pairing and admin bootstrap
items.short_title: Interview: device pairing and admin bootstrap

note_records.text: **2026-10-13** — Owner answers 2026-10-13: bootstrap by log link (single use, replaced on restart) and CLI 'python -m larder pair --person NAME'; pairing by QR (segno, approved) + link, 10 min single use; links printed as path only; cookie 1 year sliding; members get 403 on admin pages; unpaired devices get a friendly 401 page; bootstrap picks an admin from config; startup fails with no admin. Recorded in ADR 0010 and S07.

**2026-10-13** — Decisions: invalid, used or expired pairing links all get one plain 404 page (410 would say which). Pair confirm page: GET never consumes; POST consumes in db.transaction and sets cookie, 303 to /. Admin check runs inside the guard, so members get 403 before the CSRF check. Session key file is created by writing a 0600 temp file and os.link into place (atomic); a key under 32 bytes is a ConfigError. Session cookie class overrides get_cookie_secure to follow request.scheme (ProxyFix aware). pairing_token CHECK: kind=bootstrap or (person_id and expires_at not null). pyproject package-data gains web/templates/*/*.html for admin/devices.html. QR is segno svg_inline with omitsize and white background; no style attributes. Unused bootstrap tokens are also deleted at start once an admin device exists. segno 1.6.6, BSD-3-Clause, pinned in requirements.txt.

**2026-10-13** — Review fixes: a bootstrap link is now dead once an admin device exists, at GET (peek) and at POST (rechecked inside the pairing transaction, consume rolled back); MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH 1 MiB so oversized POSTs to /pair/... get 413; OSError on secrets/session_key becomes a ConfigError naming the path (clean exit 2); ADR 0010 now says tokens are looked up by hash and only CSRF tokens use constant-time compare; the no-bootstrap test now leaves the bootstrap token unused so it covers the delete-on-restart branch.

**2026-10-13** — Gate PASS (opus/medium) after one fix round: M1 dead bootstrap link once an admin device exists (peek + consume with rollback), T1 non-vacuous bootstrap cleanup test, L1 MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH 1 MiB, L2 session_key OSError -> ConfigError, ADR wording. Open lows: 413 uses Flask's default page (no error.html handler); the 1 MiB limit is app-wide and undocumented, raise it for any upload feature; AGENTS.md status line still says 'no features yet'.

**2026-11-04** — Paired devices now get a placeholder landing page at / (home.index): a You're paired heading and tonight's planned meal when there is one (planner_db.meal_on). Unpaired devices still get the 401 page; a completed pairing now lands on a 200 page. Verified with 156 passing tests, ruff clean, and seven mutation checks that each went red.

note_records.text: **2026-10-12** — From the S05 review: trusted_proxies matching does not unwrap IPv4-mapped peers. On a dual-stack bind (--host :: or a WSGI server listening on ::) an IPv4 proxy appears as ::ffff:a.b.c.d and does not match an IPv4 entry, so forwarded headers are ignored (fails closed). Unwrap address.ipv4_mapped in larder.web._is_trusted, or document listing the mapped form.

**2026-10-13** — From S07 review: every worker that calls create_app runs ensure_bootstrap. With a multi-worker WSGI server without preload, each worker logs its own /pair link, only the last works, and a respawn replaces a link the admin is about to use. Run create_app once (preload or single worker) or move bootstrap to a pre-start step (src/larder/web/__init__.py create_app).

**2026-11-04** — 2026-11-03 roadmap review: the two notes above (IPv4-mapped trusted_proxies peers; every worker running ensure_bootstrap) moved to S63 and are no longer part of this slice. S28 depends on S63. Scheduler: S64 provides it; this slice only starts it from the WSGI entrypoint.

goals:
- G1: Answer "what's for dinner?" in seconds, from meals the household actually makes.
- G2: One shared shopping list that every household member trusts.
- G3: Reduce waste and duplicate purchases using order data instead of manual logging (Phase 2).
- G4: Near-zero required upkeep; optional taps improve accuracy, none are required.
- G5: Usable by non-technical household members without help.
- G6: Portable: any household can run it with its own stores, sources and network (ADR 0015, 0016).
- G7: Reachable by message from anywhere: email or Matrix to add to the list, ask what's low, and answer larder's pantry questions (Phase 2; ADR 0025).
non_goals:
- NG1: Placing store orders automatically.
- NG2: Nutrition or calorie tracking.
- NG3: Access from the public internet.
- NG4: Multi-household or hosted operation in the MVP (future direction, ADR 0016).
- NG5: Exact, item-by-item inventory tracking.
